review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the repo for uses of regDirichletDensity. The density is defined as an `indicator` of a set, but the file has no canonical membership-split lemmas for it. Every consumer unfolds the definition and applies `Set.indicator_of_mem` or `Set.indicator_of_notMem` by hand, in this file and in ParameterShift.lean, IntegrationByParts.lean and Polynomial.lean. I did not look for other simp-interface problems in detail. I found no rewrite-direction problems or cycles, and I did not recommend simp on identities that merely look simple. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma names are suggestions that have not been compiled.

findings.excerpt: stdSimplexInterior.indicator (fun u ↦ ∏ i, (u i : ℂ) ^ (b i - 1) / Gamma (b i)) u
findings.problem: The density is an `indicator`, but there are no canonical conditional equations for it. A `@[simp]` lemma `regDirichletDensity_of_notMem (hu : u ∉ stdSimplexInterior) : regDirichletDensity b u = 0` and a lemma `regDirichletDensity_of_mem (hu : u ∈ stdSimplexInterior) : regDirichletDensity b u = ∏ i, (u i : ℂ) ^ (b i - 1) / Gamma (b i)` are both missing. Because of that, every consumer unfolds the definition and then calls `Set.indicator_of_mem` or `Set.indicator_of_notMem`. Examples are `rw [regDirichletDensity, Set.indicator_of_mem]` (line 97), `simp only [regDirichletDensity, Set.indicator_of_mem hinter, ...]` (line 139) and `rw [regDirichletDensity, Set.indicator_of_mem hinter]` (line 190). The same pattern appears in ParameterShift.lean (lines 60–61), IntegrationByParts.lean (lines 52, 70, 82) and Polynomial.lean (line 94). It exposes the `indicator` implementation detail everywhere. It also makes `simp [regDirichletDensity, hu]` rely on unfolding the definition instead of a stable rewrite rule.
findings.proposed_change: After the definition, add two lemmas. (1) `theorem regDirichletDensity_of_mem {b u} (hu : u ∈ stdSimplexInterior) : regDirichletDensity b u = ∏ i, (u i : ℂ) ^ (b i - 1) / Gamma (b i) := Set.indicator_of_mem hu _`. (2) `@[simp] theorem regDirichletDensity_of_notMem {b u} (hu : u ∉ stdSimplexInterior) : regDirichletDensity b u = 0 := Set.indicator_of_notMem hu _`. The second can be tagged `simp` because its hypothesis is discharged by hypotheses in context. `regDirichletDensity_of_mem` could be tagged `simp` as well, but only if `simp` is not expected to expand the density in unrelated goals. Then replace the manual unfold-and-indicator rewrites in this file and its downstream users with these lemmas.
findings.benefit: There is one stable interface for the two cases of the density, and downstream proofs no longer depend on the `indicator` encoding. Proofs by `by_cases hu : u ∈ stdSimplexInterior` shrink to `simp [hu]` or `rw [regDirichletDensity_of_mem hu]`, and the definition can later be changed without touching callers.
